title: Biofuel Production Overview
desc: Understand how biofuels are made from crops, waste and algae, with sustainability, safety, cost and policy.
outcomes: Explain biofuel types and basic production steps.
Do simple mass and energy balances.
Write a balanced overview for a community or investor.
task: Produce a three-page overview of one biofuel pathway with process chart, balance, emissions estimate, risks and recommendation.
condition: A computer, public data, a spreadsheet, two peers and a mentor. No production work is done.
standard: Process steps and balances are correct; emissions use stated assumptions; risks and safety are listed; sources dated; peers rate Meets or better.
who: Students, farm cooperatives, energy staff, policy assistants.
evidence: process chart, balance sheet, emissions estimate, overview
modules: Liquid and gas fuels from biomass.
Ethanol from sugar or starch; biodiesel from oils; biogas from waste.
Advanced fuels from residues and algae.
Blends: low blends are used in existing engines.
Vegetable oil waste becomes biodiesel after a simple chemical step.
Each type has feedstock and use.
Food crops, residues, used oil, energy crops.
Compare yield per hectare and competing uses.
Used cooking oil avoids new land use.
Collect, clean, convert, separate, purify, store.
Fermentation for ethanol; transesterification for biodiesel; digestion for biogas.
Co-products such as glycerol or digestate.
Digestate returns nutrients to the field.
Energy out / energy in gives a ratio.
100 kg oil gives about 95 kg biodiesel and 10 kg glycerol with alcohol.
Cleaner only if the whole chain is clean.
Count land change, fertiliser, processing energy and transport.
Compare against fossil fuel per MJ.
Waste-based fuel can cut emissions greatly; land-clearing crops may not.
Flammable liquids, methanol and acids need controls.
Quality tests: water content, acidity, flash point.
A spill kit and earthing are installed at the tank.
Incentives and blend mandates change prices.
Fair prices for farmers and no food shortages.
A mandate raises demand for used oil, so collection grows.
State what you do not know.
The note recommends biogas from market waste first.
quiz: Another useful output such as glycerol.
Name an emissions source in the chain.
rubric: Every claim linked to a dated record and checked by a peer
Checked, dated and explained to others
next: greenhouse gas auditing, plastic alternatives, wind and solar basics.
local: Fuel standards, licences and incentives differ by place.
ladder: L1: learner can name biofuel types.
L2: learner knows feedstock and hazard basics.
L3: learner can follow a process chart.
L4: learner can do a simple balance.
L7: learner can audit an overview.
